data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'fahad', meaning 'to let go, to release, to free'. In Islamic contexts, it symbolizes spiritual liberation and emancipation from worldly desires. The name Fuhaidaa carries the meaning “Liberated, freed” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fuhaidaa usually hope their child will grow to embody liberated, freed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
